answer: Each winter the fishmonger cuts ice and stores it in the ice house, and every block is counted at the door and entered in the tally before the fish may be packed. A relic block hauled from another town fails the tally: at the fable of the ice house the blocks must match the tally's own count, and a strange block melts before the fish reaches market. Faking the ice means cutting ice for a month, hauling 600 blocks and paying 8,200, while the velvet figure in the tally is read at every packing, so fish whose ice was never counted is left to spoil.
